## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, responsive mobile puzzle game for Android, with smooth touch controls and a minimalist UI.

## Requirements
- Include score tracking, a timer, and a restart button; keep gameplay lightweight and touchscreen-friendly.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Workspace was a blank project, so the assistant chose a 2048-style sliding-number puzzle.
- Implemented as a standalone web app with swipe, keyboard, and tap controls; added undo, persistent best score/game state, optional sound, and installable/offline PWA support.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game UI, gameplay logic, styling, PWA manifest, icon, and service worker.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Started the app with `./start.sh` in a tmux session; `http://localhost:3000/` returned HTTP 200.
- Opened the app in Playwright and resized viewport to 412×915.

### Active
- Finish browser/screenshot verification; save and inspect a latest JPEG (at most 1280px wide).
- Test a move, score/timer behavior, and mobile layout if possible.

### Blocked
- Playwright’s expected Chromium binary was initially missing; it was symlinked to `/usr/bin/chromium`, and Playwright then opened successfully.
- Screenshot conversion via PIL failed because PIL is not installed; use Playwright’s JPEG screenshot support instead.

## Next Move
1. Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=/tmp/opencode/slideclub.jpg --type=jpeg` at the current 412×915 viewport and inspect the resulting image.
2. Check the browser snapshot/console and exercise controls; fix any issues found.
3. Report assumptions and verification results to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game structure and visible UI.
